```{python}
# Load in necessary tables
shoppers = pl.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuibigdata/app_challenge_wi26_hathaway/main/data/cstore_shopper.parquet")
stores = pl.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuibigdata/app_challenge_wi26_hathaway/main/data/cstore_stores.parquet")
sets = pl.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuibigdata/app_challenge_wi26_hathaway/main/data/cstore_transaction_sets.parquet")
items0 = pl.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuibigdata/app_challenge_wi26_hathaway/main/data/transaction_items/part-00000.parquet")
items1 = pl.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuibigdata/app_challenge_wi26_hathaway/main/data/transaction_items/part-00001.parquet")
items2 = pl.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuibigdata/app_challenge_wi26_hathaway/main/data/transaction_items/part-00002.parquet")
items3 = pl.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuibigdata/app_challenge_wi26_hathaway/main/data/transaction_items/part-00003.parquet")
items4 = pl.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuibigdata/app_challenge_wi26_hathaway/main/data/transaction_items/part-00004.parquet")
items5 = pl.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuibigdata/app_challenge_wi26_hathaway/main/data/transaction_items/part-00005.parquet")
items6 = pl.read_parquet("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byuibigdata/app_challenge_wi26_hathaway/main/data/transaction_items/part-00006.parquet")

# Create baseline tables

# Merge items tables

items = (
    items0
    .union(items1)
    .union(items2)
    .union(items3)
    .union(items4)
    .union(items5)
    .union(items6)
)

# Join shoppers, transactions, items, and stores tables
joined_items = (shoppers
                .join(transactions, on = "TRANSACTION_SET_ID", how = "left")
                .join(stores, "STORE_ID", how = "left")
                .withColumn("MONTH", sf.month("DATE_TIME"))
                .withColumn("YEAR", sf.year("DATE_TIME"))
                .join(items, "GTIN", how = "left"))

# Join shoppers, sets, and stores table. Create columns for year, month, and hour of each transaction set
joined_sets = (shoppers
               .join(sets, on = "TRANSACTION_SET_ID", how = "left")
               .join(stores, on = "STORE_ID", how = "left")
               .withColumn("MONTH", sf.month("DATE_TIME"))
               .withColumn("YEAR", sf.year("DATE_TIME"))
               .withColumn("TIME", sf.hour("DATE_TIME")))
```

I took convenience store sales data and created a couple of features that would be used by a clustering model to segment a convenience store's customer base. Data came from Dewey Data. I used PySpark to perform all the engineering. 

The first feature is the number of cycles it has been since the customer last shop. A cycle is the average number of days between visits.
